questions.text: Consider a quadratic equation [latex]x^{2} -13x +36 = 0[/latex] with coefficients in a base b. The solutions of this equation in the same base b are x = 5 and x = 6. Then b = ___________.
questions.solution:
In base b: 13 = b + 3 and 36 = 3b + 6. Sum of roots: 5 + 6 = 11 = b + 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] b = 8. Check product: 30 = 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 + 6 True

Answer: 8

questions.text:
Let [latex]P=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1&-1 \\ 2&-3 & 4\\ 3 &-2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] Q=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -2&-1 \\ 6 & 12& 6\\ 5&10 & 5 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] be two matrices.
Then the rank of P +Q is _____________.
questions.solution:
[latex]P+Q=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1&-2\\8&9&10\\8&8&8\end{bmatrix}[/latex]. Row 2 = Row 3 [latex]-[/latex] Row 1, so the rows are dependent; rows 1 and 3 are independent.

Rank = 2

Answer: 2

questions.text: If [latex]f(x)=R sin(\frac{\pi x}{2})+S,f'(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{2}[/latex] and [latex] \int_{0}^{1}f(x)dx=\frac{2R}{\pi }[/latex], then the constants R and S are, respectively
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]f'(x)=\frac{R\pi}{2}\cos\frac{\pi x}{2}[/latex], so [latex]f'(\tfrac12)=\frac{R\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2\Rightarrow R=\frac4\pi[/latex]
- [latex]\int_0^1f\,dx=R\cdot\frac2\pi+S[/latex]. This equals [latex]\frac{2R}{\pi}[/latex], so S = 0.

Answer: [latex]\frac4\pi[/latex] and 0

questions.text:
Let A be nxn real valued square symmetric matrix of rank 2 with [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}A^{2}_{ij}=50[/latex]. Consider the following statements.

(I) One eigen value must be in [-5, 5]
(II) The eigen value with the largest magnitude must be strictly greater than 5.

Which of the above statements about eigen values of A is/are necessarily CORRECT?
questions.solution:
A is symmetric with rank 2, so it has two non-zero eigenvalues [latex]\lambda_1,\lambda_2[/latex] (the rest are 0), and [latex]\sum A_{ij}^2=\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex].

- (I): [latex]\lambda_1^2+\lambda_2^2=50[/latex] forces one of them to have [latex]|\lambda|\le5[/latex] (and the zero eigenvalues are in [[latex]-[/latex]5, 5] anyway) True
- (II): [latex]\lambda_1=\lambda_2=5[/latex] gives 50, and the largest is not strictly greater than 5 False

Answer: (I) only

questions.text: Let u and v be two vectors in [latex]R^{2}[/latex] whose Euclidean norms satisfy ||u||=2|| v|| . What is the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] such that w=u+[latex]\alpha[/latex]v bisects the angle between u and v ?
questions.solution:
The bisector points along the sum of the unit vectors: [latex]\frac{u}{\|u\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{u}{2\|v\|}+\frac{v}{\|v\|}=\frac{1}{2\|v\|}(u+2v)[/latex].

So w = u + 2v bisects the angle: [latex]\alpha=2[/latex].

Answer: 2
